normalized.quote: Now she’s 30, and her private, Palo Alto-based corporation, called Theranos–the name is an amalgam of the words “therapy” and “diagnosis”–has 500 employees and has raised more than $400 million from equity sales to investors who have effectively valued the company at more than $9 billion.

facts: Elizabeth Holmes founded Theranos after dropping out of Stanford University in the fall of 2003.
Theranos is a Palo Alto-based corporation that has raised more than $400 million and is valued at over $9 billion by investors.
The company operates a high-complexity laboratory certified by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS).
Theranos tests can be performed on small blood samples of 25 to 50 microliters collected via a finger stick into a vial called a nanotainer.
Theranos prices are often a half to a quarter of independent lab prices and are set to never exceed half the Medicare reimbursement rate.
Walgreens partnered with Theranos to establish diagnostic collection centers in its drugstores.
